elements.meaning: A node-based binary tree data structure with the following properties:

elements.title: Properties
items: The left subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys lesser than the node's key.
The right subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys greater than the node's key.
The left and right subtree each must also be a binary search tree.

elements.text: Search time complexity in a balanced BST is O(log n).

elements.meaning: A binary search tree where the height of the left and right subtrees of every node differs by at most one.

elements.title: Search Algorithm
steps: Compare the target key with the root node's key
If the target key is less than the root node's key, go left
If the target key is greater than the root node's key, go right
If the target key is equal to the root node's key, return the node
If the target key is not found, return null

elements.text: To maintain the BST property, insertions and deletions must be done in a way that preserves the BST property.

elements.meaning: The process of adding a new node to the BST.
The process of removing a node from the BST.

elements.title: Insertion Algorithm
steps: Compare the new node's key with the root node's key
If the new node's key is less than the root node's key, go left
If the new node's key is greater than the root node's key, go right
If the new node's key is equal to the root node's key, update the node's value
If the new node's key is not found, insert the new node as a leaf node

elements.title: Deletion Algorithm
steps: Start at the node to be deleted
If the node has no children, delete the node
If the node has one child, replace the node with its child
If the node has two children, find the node's in-order successor or predecessor and replace the node with it

points: A binary search tree is a node-based binary tree data structure with the following properties: the left subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys lesser than the node's key, the right subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys greater than the node's key, and the left and right subtree each must also be a binary search tree.
Search time complexity in a balanced BST is O(log n).
To maintain the BST property, insertions and deletions must be done in a way that preserves the BST property.
